summary: Rory Brendan Lindsay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and completed his PhD at Harvard University, supervised by Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.
Rory Mackenzie works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed doctoral studies under the supervision of Peter Harvey and held a teaching post at International Christian College.

Rosalind O'Hanlon is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. After earning her PhD at SOAS University of London (~1977–1982), she held posts at Clare College, Cambridge (~1988–2006) and the University of Oxford (~2006–2021).

Rosan Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from 1960 to ~1969. He served Komazawa University as assistant, lecturer, associate professor, and professor (1969–2012), and directed the Soto Zen Research Center in 2009.

Rosane Rocher is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Free University of Brussels under Ludo Rocher. She worked at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1961–1970) before becoming a professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 1970.

Rosemarie Fuchs is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Katia Holmes and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, and served as a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).

Rosemarie Lühr is a linguist and Indologist who earned her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nuremberg. She held posts at the University of Regensburg, University of Giessen, University of Jena (1994–2013), and Humboldt University of Berlin.
Rosemary Radford Ruether was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. She studied at Claremont School of Theology (~1960–1965) and held an academic post at Howard University from ~1965 to 1975.

Rosina Pastore is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She earned her PhD at the University of Lausanne, supervised by Maya Burger and Stefania Cavaliere, and has held research posts at Lausanne and Ghent University.

Ross Bolleter is a Buddhist studies scholar and Zen Buddhist teacher. He earned his bachelor's degree at the University of Western Australia, trained under Robert Baker Aitken and John Tarrant, and taught at the Zen Group of Western Australia (~1983–2023).

Roy Rappaport was a scholar of religious studies who completed his doctorate at Columbia University (~1959–1966). He served at the University of Michigan (~1965–1997) as Chair of the Department of Anthropology.

Roy Tzohar is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tel Aviv University and earned a PhD from Columbia University under Gary A. Tubb (~2004–2011). He joined the faculty of Tel Aviv University around 2011.

Roy W. Perrett is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at the University of Canterbury and the University of Otago (~1978–1981). He held academic posts at Massey University (~1987–2003), the University of Melbourne, and the University of Hawaiʻi (~2003).

Royall Tyler is a Japanologist who studied at Harvard and Columbia, completing a doctorate under Donald Keene. He taught at Ohio State, Wisconsin-Madison, the University of Oslo, and the Australian National University (1990–2000), later visiting Harvard.
Royce Wiles is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the Australian National University by 2000 and subsequently held a post at the same institution.

Ruben L. F. Habito is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Jikidō Takasaki. He held posts at Sophia University, Southern Methodist University, and Ryukoku University.
Rudolf G. Wagner was a sinologist who studied at Bonn, Paris, Munich, and Heidelberg. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin (~1972–1987) and Heidelberg University (~1987–2019).

Rudolf Haym was a scholar of philosophy and history who studied at the Köllnisches Gymnasium, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and Frederick William University Berlin. He held a post at the University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1868.

Rudolf Kaschewsky was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Cologne and Bonn, worked at the University of Bonn (1974–2004), and taught Tibetan at Goethe University Frankfurt.
Rudolf Lange was a scholar in Japanology and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1874–1881) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1887–1920).
